answer: Sealed-bid admission auction: each identity bids once for one island plot; only top bids win. Each bid is sealed in umber wax, hiding prices; after opening, all bids go public, and a copied bid burns the 70-credit bond. First plot 42, k-th 42+8(k-1): 1,000 fakes pay 4,038,000, locking 70,000 more for a 40,000 pool. Rented bids fail on a juniper grove: one key, one bid, duplicate seals void both. An honest agent bids 42 once and keeps its plot.
